lag_pins.why: status return: the head configures every leaf (cfg landed +3 into each leaf region) and ORs their sticky faults / checks their valid lockstep; that is a cross-region loop, so the status inputs are landed back and read at one common lag (all leaves alike: no false lockstep fault)

bench.why: load phase (cycles < 8000: a configuration write on half the edges, every row / local bank) then run phase (starts 1 in 40, rare writes 1 in 100 so the write-on-start leaf fault rises late and is compared through the lagged status path)

mut_waivers.4: PL-PSLICE bench 10-18: MUT 4 (the first reset child's reset run one stage long) PASSES lockstep over 20,000 edges because every child of this parent is reset-phase-insensitive: no free-running state (the producer is idle until a start; SRAM is not reset), so one more reset edge is invisible unless a write lands on exactly that edge. The reset offsets themselves are proven by MUT 0 (every child reset delayed t(child) + RB) and the flat-eq bench.

why_reader_per_inst: TW2-PSLICE2 real7 10-19: real6 (CTS PASS, GRT ovf 0) failed setup -870 ps / TNS -364 ns on 1,453 read registers: one read half per REGION sat by wirelength next to the head's ring (l/t readers at x 224..590 although their leaves span 43..1857), so the same-root rc -> 8:1 mux -> o path and o -> far leaf ran ~1-2 mm in one cycle, and the l/t/b soft flops sat ~1 mm from the region's children (per-pair clock spread h 96 / l 168 / t ~364 / b 143 ps TT). Now every reader leaf has its own read half beside it (kit fence) and ONE ring per (net, source region) beside the head is read by all of them: the long hop is the multicycle ring -> read bank (E = 3), offsets / K / D / E unchanged, ring flops 3x fewer.

regional_reset_ports.why: L2H-PSLICE r8: each region's reset lands beside its own pin on its own root (2 landing stages) + 1 reach relay (the L leaf is 453.6 um tall: pin on the command face, every reset sink -- read halves, child rst_n -- on the cfg face); same depth in every region so all landing epochs start on one edge

why_regions: real7 per-root child-flop spread TT h 97 / l 568 / t 286 / b 156 ps: a root spanning several leaves (t: 5 leaves 1.7 mm; l: 3 L leaves 1.1 mm) cannot hold <= 80 ps between soft landing flops and child flops; one root per leaf keeps every tree inside one leaf footprint
